headline: ENCORE ENERGY WINS BLM INFRASTRUCTURE APPROVAL AT DEWEY BURDOCK — SOUTH DAKOTA'S FIRST ISR URANIUM MINE CLEARS FINAL CONSTRUCTION HURDLE
source_name: Investing News Network / enCore Energy Corp. (NYSE American: EU)
snippet: enCore Energy Corp. (NYSE American: EU) announced June 18, 2026 receipt of Bureau of Land Management authorization to begin construction of all surface infrastructure required at its Dewey Burdock In-Situ Recovery uranium project in the southern Black Hills of South Dakota — including access roads, monitoring wells, and power lines — the final federal construction permit needed before site preparation can commence. Dewey Burdock holds a 28-year ISR mine life and targets initial production of approximately 1 million pounds U3O8 per year, with the NRC source material license already in hand after a decade of regulatory development. South Dakota has never hosted an operating ISR uranium mine; the BLM authorization makes Dewey Burdock the only ISR uranium project in the state with full federal surface rights cleared for construction. With US uranium spot near $86/lb and US utilities under-contracted through the early 2030s, a fully permitted, NRC-licensed ISR project now cleared for construction in a new US uranium state represents one of the more precisely defined near-term production additions available in the domestic uranium supply chain — at a moment when the US Commerce Secretary faces a June 30 decision on copper tariffs that signals escalating administration interest in critical mineral self-sufficiency.

headline: VIZSLA COPPER SPINS UP 2 RIGS AT ALASKA'S PALMER VMS — 10,000m SOUTH WALL ZONE CAMPAIGN TARGETS CU-ZN-AG CORE
source_name: Investing News Network / Vizsla Copper Corp. (TSXV: VCU)
snippet: Vizsla Copper Corp. (TSXV: VCU) announced June 18, 2026 the commencement of its 2026 drill program at the Palmer Project in southeast Alaska — a $19.2 million, 10,000-metre, two-rig campaign running June through September and targeting the copper-zinc-silver core of the South Wall Zone within the Palmer volcanogenic massive sulphide system. The Palmer VMS deposit is one of the highest-grade undeveloped copper-silver systems in North America; the South Wall Zone represents the richest sector of the deposit and the primary focus for expanding the resource envelope ahead of a planned preliminary economic assessment. In a copper market pricing a potential 15% Section 232 tariff by June 30 — with the US Commerce Secretary facing that deadline on refined copper import duties — a fully domestic, Alaska-domiciled high-grade copper-zinc VMS system commencing a major drill program is precisely the kind of North American copper development story that institutional investors and government procurement programs are tracking ahead of the tariff regime's implementation. Southeast Alaska's infrastructure position, tidewater access, and established mining regulatory framework differentiate Palmer from exploration-stage peers in remote jurisdictions with less defined logistics pathways.

headline: FREEGOLD VENTURES DRILLS 336.8m @ 1.32 g/t Au FROM 26.5m AT GOLDEN SUMMIT — WIDE SHALLOW INTERCEPTS ANCHOR ALASKA PFS INFILL
source_name: Investing News Network / Freegold Ventures Limited (TSX: FVL)
snippet: Freegold Ventures Limited (TSX: FVL) announced June 17, 2026 new infill drill results from its Golden Summit gold project in Interior Alaska — with hole GS2562 returning 336.8 metres at 1.32 g/t Au from 26.5 metres depth, including a higher-grade interval of 36.0 metres at 2.37 g/t Au, and a second hole delivering 185.8 metres at 1.08 g/t Au. The results are part of a 50,000-metre, six-rig Pre-Feasibility Study drilling campaign designed to increase resource confidence and tighten the block model for the PFS. Golden Summit hosts a large, low-strip open-pit bulk-tonnage gold system in the Fairbanks district of Alaska; the project's PFS-stage economics are being defined at current gold prices substantially above the $1,800–2,000/oz levels at which most comparable Interior Alaska systems were last evaluated. Wide shallow intercepts from surface — 336 metres of gold mineralisation beginning at just 26.5 metres depth — confirm the low-strip, low-waste geometry that drives open-pit economics, while the six-rig campaign pace signals a company moving deliberately toward a fundable feasibility study at a gold price that makes Alaskan open-pit development economics structurally more compelling than at any point in the project's history.

headline: CASSIAR GOLD OPENS 10,000m PHASE 1 AT TAURUS — HISTORIC 315,000 oz HIGH-GRADE BC VEINS IN DRILL SIGHTS FOR FIRST TIME IN YEARS
source_name: Investing News Network / Cassiar Gold Corp. (TSXV: GLDC)
snippet: Cassiar Gold Corp. (TSXV: GLDC) announced June 18, 2026 the commencement of its 2026 exploration program with a 10,000-metre Phase 1 drill campaign at the Taurus Deposit and Cassiar South target on its Cassiar property in northwest British Columbia. The Cassiar South historic vein system produced approximately 315,000 ounces at high grades of 10–20 g/t Au from underground operations, and the current program represents the first systematic modern drilling of these high-grade structures with contemporary 3D targeting methods. The Taurus Deposit is the primary NI 43-101 resource target; the historic Cassiar South veins are a parallel high-grade discovery target that, if confirmed at depth with modern drilling, would represent a discovery catalyst on top of the ongoing resource advancement program. Northwest BC's established mining infrastructure corridor — shared with the Golden Triangle and Toodoggone districts — provides the logistical foundation for exploring a district that has seen limited modern systematic drilling despite a documented high-grade production history. For investors tracking BC gold explorers in the current $4,155/oz gold environment, a 10-20 g/t historic production grade combined with a systematic modern first-pass drill campaign is the setup that precedes the most significant single-hole discovery outcomes available in the Canadian junior sector.

headline: K2 GOLD DEFINES 5 WALKER LANE TARGETS AT Si2 — 73m DISSEMINATED ZONE AND EPITHERMAL VEINS ACROSS 1.4km NEVADA CORRIDOR
source_name: Investing News Network / K2 Gold Corporation (TSXV: KTO)
snippet: K2 Gold Corporation (TSXV: KTO) reported June 18, 2026 results from its Si2 Project in Nevada's Walker Lane mineral belt — identifying five Areas of Interest spanning a 1,450-metre corridor with both disseminated and epithermal vein-hosted gold-silver mineralisation styles. Best results include 73.15 metres at 0.117 g/t Au (including 9.14 metres at 0.206 g/t Au) in the disseminated zone and gold-silver quartz veins confirmed across multiple holes. The five AOIs are spaced 600 to 1,450 metres apart, suggesting a large-footprint low-sulphidation epithermal system where individual high-grade vein shoots remain to be discovered within the broader mineralised corridor. Nevada's Walker Lane is the US's most productive precious metals corridor — hosting bonanza-grade epithermal deposits including the Comstock, Goldstrike, and Round Mountain systems — and a five-AOI system with 1.4km of defined corridor and dual mineralisation styles at the initial drill stage is the footprint geometry that precedes the most significant Walker Lane discoveries. The disseminated halo grades establish the structural corridor's mineralisation competence while vein intercepts define the high-grade targets that subsequent phases will systematically test.

headline: CRITICAL METALS DRILLS TANBREEZ — 10,000m CAMPAIGN OPENS AT ONE OF WORLD'S LARGEST UNDEVELOPED REE PROJECTS IN GREENLAND
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Critical Metals Corp. (Nasdaq: CRML)
snippet: Critical Metals Corp. (Nasdaq: CRML) announced June 17, 2026 the commencement of a 10,000-metre drilling campaign at its Tanbreez rare earth project in southern Greenland — one of the world's largest undeveloped rare earth deposits, with a focus on heavy rare earth elements including dysprosium, terbium, and holmium that are most strategically critical for permanent magnet applications and US defence supply chain independence. Infrastructure at Tanbreez has been commissioned and is operational; the 2026 program is designed to advance the resource dataset toward a Preliminary Economic Assessment. Greenland's rare earth geology is among the world's richest — the Ilímaussaq alkaline complex hosts Kvanefjeld, Kringlerne, and Tanbreez in a cluster of globally significant HREE deposits — while the 2024 US-Greenland Critical Minerals MOU and elevated US government interest in Greenland's strategic resources has materially improved the sovereign risk profile for Greenland-based developers. In the context of the Pentagon's active REE capital deployment — including the US$725 million DoD conditional loan to Energy Fuels announced this week — a Nasdaq-listed developer advancing the world's largest undeveloped HREE system with infrastructure already commissioned represents one of the highest-leverage positions available in the ex-China HREE supply chain.

headline: RELEVANT GOLD'S VTEM MAPS 44 WYOMING ANOMALIES — LEWISTON CORRIDOR RUNS 3km+ AT DEPTH IN SOUTH PASS PRECAMBRIAN TERRANE
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Relevant Gold Corp. (TSXV: RGC)
snippet: Relevant Gold Corp. (TSXV: RGC) reported June 18, 2026 results from a 2,807 line-kilometre VTEM airborne electromagnetic survey at its South Pass gold project in Wyoming — identifying 44 EM anomalies across the property, with 15 classified as high-priority drill targets including the Lewiston corridor, which exhibits more than 3 kilometres of strike at more than 400 metres depth. South Pass is one of Wyoming's most historically productive gold districts, with documented placer and lode production from the Precambrian greenstone terrane stretching back to the 19th century; the Lewiston structure is a bedrock-hosted lode target within the same structural system. A 2,807 line-km airborne geophysical survey defining a 3km+ structural corridor at depth — in a documented Wyoming gold district that has seen limited modern systematic exploration — is the dataset that allows a junior to move from conceptual reconnaissance to drill-ready target prioritisation in a single field season. The 44 anomaly inventory gives the program a multi-year drill pipeline from a single geophysics campaign, at a gold price that makes Wyoming lode gold development economics more compelling than at any prior point in South Pass's exploration history.

headline: SILVER'S 47% CRASH FROM $121 ATH IS THE SETUP, NOT THE STORY — MALONEY ORG FRAMES CORRECTION AS STRUCTURAL DEMAND COIL
snippet: GoldSilver.com published June 16, 2026 a silver price outlook framing the current 47% correction from January's $121/oz all-time high as a structural setup rather than a trend reversal — arguing that the FOMC's hawkish hold and dollar strength represent near-term headwinds rather than fundamental demand destruction, while the industrial silver demand base from solar, EVs, and defence electronics continues to grow regardless of speculative positioning. The analysis distinguishes between speculative silver (liquidating through ETF redemptions and futures position reduction) and physical industrial silver (tight, with fabrication demand running ahead of mine supply), arguing that when speculative positioning clears — as it appears to be doing in the current $64–65/oz range — the structural industrial bid will reassert from a cleaner baseline. For junior silver mining investors holding producers and explorers down 40–60% from January, the framework offers a demand-side anchor for the contrarian accumulation thesis: the same industrial megatrends that drove silver's January ATH have not reversed — only the speculative premium has corrected — suggesting the next advance will be built on a more durable foundation than the first. Jeffrey Christian of CPM Group's concurrent June 16 analysis targeting a possible $60 floor provides the bear case bracket; GoldSilver.com's framework provides the structural demand counter-argument.

headline: AI DATA CENTRES, MINE FLOODS, AND JUNE 30 TARIFFS: DEVERE MAPS THE 2026 COPPER CRUNCH — UBS TARGETS $14,000/t BY SEPTEMBER
snippet: DeVere Group published June 16, 2026 a mid-year copper market analysis synthesising four simultaneous supply-demand drivers compressing into the second half of 2026: AI data centre build-out consuming copper at a rate not anticipated in any 2025 supply model; the Kamoa-Kakula flooding in the DRC and El Teniente underground accident in Chile removing material supply from an already-tight market; the June 30 deadline for the US Commerce Secretary to deliver a Section 232 recommendation on 15% (2027) and 30% (2028) refined copper import tariffs; and a structural deficit now projected by Morgan Stanley at approximately 600,000 tonnes. UBS's target of US$14,000 per metric tonne by September 2026 — against the current sub-$6.30/lb ($13,890/t) spot price following Oyu Tolgoi's resumption — implies the supply disruption premium has not yet been fully priced. For copper equity investors, the analysis provides a framework for the June 30 tariff catalyst: a Section 232 recommendation confirming 15% tariffs would immediately re-rate North American copper producers (Hudbay, First Quantum Canadian assets, Copper Mountain/New Ingerbelle) as tariff-protected supply sources at a moment when the structural deficit makes domestic copper supply — not just domestic processing — strategically valuable.
